name: poll_margin_error
description: Margin of error of a poll proportion at any confidence level, with finite-population correction and design effect; the sample size needed for a target margin; and whether the lead between two candidates in the same poll exceeds sampling error, using the multinomial variance of the difference.

p.description: Proportion, 0.52 or "52%"; 0.5 gives the widest margin

population.description: Population size for the finite-population correction

design_effect.description: Variance inflation from weighting or clustering

margin.description: Target margin of error, 0.03 or "3%", for the required sample size

p1.description: First candidate's share in the poll

p2.description: Second candidate's share in the same poll

catalog.source: original; normal quantile by P. J. Acklam's algorithm with a Halley refinement; finite-population correction and design effect as in Kish, Survey Sampling (1965); lead variance from the multinomial covariance of two shares; checked against Wikipedia's Margin of error article and Python's statistics.NormalDist
